clue.text: Missile covered in report

parts.note: a bullet is a missile fired from a gun

explanation.surface: A rocket or shell is mentioned in a news report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' just links the missile to the plain word 'in' that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official statement or news broadcast, a kind of report.

clue.text: Twice contracting fungal growth in the arm

parts.note: the prefix bi-, meaning twice, is a shortened form of the Latin bis
ceps are edible wild mushrooms, the porcini

explanation.surface: Something about a fungus growing twice over on someone's arm, like a nasty infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracting' looks like a muscle flexing but tells you 'twice' is shortened to its prefix form.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is the large muscle found at the front of the upper arm, so it is what lies in that limb.

clue.text: Burglar lashes Tory leader! That's most malicious!

parts.note: a cat burglar is often just called a cat
to lash is to tie or bind, so lashes means ties

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from Tory

explanation.surface: A burglar whips the head of the Conservative party, an act of supreme spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Catty means spiteful, so its superlative describes the most spiteful or malicious person.

clue.text: World's energy consumed by factory

indicators.note: something consumed by another is swallowed up inside it, so the letter goes into the factory word

parts.note: a plant is an industrial factory
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A complaint that the planet's energy is being eaten up by industry.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after World stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A world is a planet, such as Earth or Mars orbiting a star.

clue.text: Workshop produces ornament I love

parts.note: a stud is a small decorative ornament, as in an earring
love means zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A craft workshop turns out a decoration that the speaker adores.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a room where an artist or craftsperson works, a kind of workshop.

clue.text: Password for man entering bishopric

indicators.note: the man goes into the bishop's district, so his name sits inside it

parts.note: a see is the diocese or seat of a bishop
Sam is a typical man's name

explanation.surface: A secret word that lets a man into a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Open sesame is the magic phrase from Ali Baba, so the word has become a byword for a password.

clue.text: Diva cries about article

indicators.note: the cries go round the article, so the short word sits within them

parts.note: calls are cries or shouts
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A prima donna shouts about some newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Callas was a famous Greek-American soprano, the archetypal opera diva.

clue.text: Agent commandeers shelter for dwarf

indicators.note: to commandeer is to seize and hold, so the agent holds the shelter inside

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A secret agent seizes a refuge meant for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy is one of the seven dwarfs in the Snow White story.

clue.text: Bill carries a bird in a lift

indicators.note: the bill holds the other pieces within it, as if carrying them

parts.note: a bill is a printed notice or poster
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A poster shows a bird inside an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: A paternoster is a lift of open cars moving continuously in a loop, like rosary beads.

clue.text: Irish leader disposed of drug for operatic heroine

indicators.note: the leader of the word Irish is its first letter

parts.note: goods disposed of in a sale have been sold
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An Irish chief got rid of narcotics, all to do with an opera's heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the heroine of Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde, herself an Irish princess.

clue.text: Was there when a Rechabite expired

parts.note: Rechabites were a temperance society, so a Rechabite is teetotal, abbreviated TT
something that has expired has ended

explanation.surface: Someone was present at the death of a teetotal member of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: To have attended an event is to have been present at it.

clue.text: Repulsive material makes stomachs turn

indicators.note: to turn the word round is to read it backwards

parts.note: tums is informal for stomachs

explanation.surface: Disgusting content makes people feel queasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is indecent or obscene matter, which many find offensive.

clue.text: See pottery modified to a set form

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Look how this ceramic ware has been reshaped into a standard mould.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype is a fixed, conventional image, and originally a solid printing plate cast from a mould.

clue.text: Epitome of a popular motor race

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a motor is a car
a race is a people, a nation

explanation.surface: The ultimate example of a well-loved Grand Prix event.
explanation.definitionFit: An incarnation is a living embodiment of a quality, just as an epitome is its perfect example.

clue.text: Philanthropy is a liberal axiom

parts.note: a truism is a self-evident truth, an axiom

explanation.surface: Giving generously is a principle held by liberal thinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is selfless concern for others, which is what charitable love of mankind amounts to.

clue.text: Reporter of outside broadcast on tennis player

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: the server is the tennis player starting a point

explanation.surface: A journalist covers a televised match featuring a tennis star.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer watches and reports on events, like a correspondent or reporter.

clue.text: Endorse Anglo-French compact

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for Anglo
firm means solid or compact

explanation.surface: Approval is given for a treaty between Britain and France.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to state support for something, to confirm or endorse it.

clue.text: Drink with Kansas leaders in Kansas

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily
the leading letters of the word Kansas are K and A

explanation.surface: A toast with the state's political bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Topeka is the state capital, a city located in that Midwestern US state.

clue.text: Star at fete produced a sensational finish

indicators.note: the letters are produced in a fresh arrangement, like a staged show

explanation.surface: A celebrity at a village fair gave the event a thrilling climax.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftertaste is the flavour lingering after eating, a final impression on the senses.

clue.text: Demands (and gets) old book

parts.note: ex means former or old
Acts is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone insists on, and receives, an antique volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact payment is to insist on it and obtain it, as with a tax or penalty.

clue.text: European leader approved extract

indicators.note: the leader of the word European is its first letter

parts.note: licit means lawful or approved

explanation.surface: A head of a European state sanctioned an excerpt.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit a response is to draw it out, to extract it from someone.

clue.text: Small beast is lighter

parts.note: a cow is a beast of the field

explanation.surface: A tiny animal weighs less than you might think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' reads as a comparative of light, but here it is a noun: a barge.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat for carrying cargo, which is what a lighter is.

clue.text: One with gun interrupts seduction of Bond

indicators.note: a piece that interrupts another breaks into the middle of it

parts.note: a lure is an enticement or seduction
I is the Roman numeral for one
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: An armed man breaks in while James Bond is seducing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it is simply a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligature is anything used to tie or bind, so it is a bond.

clue.text: Serial broadcast in the country

indicators.note: something broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A TV series is aired nationwide.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: Inability to speak of misshapen summit

indicators.note: a misshapen word has had its letters bent out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Being lost for words about a deformed mountain top.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutism is the medical term for being unable or unwilling to talk.

clue.text: A mince pie is an art form

indicators.note: printer's pie is type jumbled together, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A claim that a festive pastry counts as an art form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' looks like part of the pastry but is the old printing word for jumbled type.
explanation.definitionFit: Film is often called the seventh art, a form of creative expression.
